subject: Post-demo: Norbio SLO/SLA follow-up — latency measurement, concurrency & reporting
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@norbio.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@norbio.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 15:08:00 -0400
Subject: Post-demo: Norbio SLO/SLA follow-up — latency measurement, concurrency & reporting

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap of what we heard on your side and a few follow-ups so we can land crisp SLO language and sizing assumptions for procurement:

What we captured from the call:
- Target interactive latency: p95 <= 300ms for single-turn text generation at 512 tokens typical request.
- Peak throughput target: ~150 requests/sec during batch inference windows (batch windows are off-peak, not UI).
- Concurrency: UI flows expect up to ~40 concurrent streaming sessions (each streaming ~1 token every ~150ms on average).
- Streaming behavior: need reliable partial-token streaming (chunked responses) and session resume for transient disconnects.
- Reporting: monthly SLO report + weekly alerting for any 72-hour degradation.

Open questions we promised to confirm:
1) Measurement basis: do you want SLOs measured at p95 or p99? (we suggested p95 for interactive UI, p99 for critical webhook flows)
2) Exclusions: do scheduled maintenance windows or major model upgrades count as exclusions?
3) Remedies: prefer SLA credits or an escalation-based engineering response with timed remedies?
4) Throughput vs reserved capacity: confirm if you need guaranteed reserved nodes vs burstable capacity.

Attached is a lightweight SLO draft (Norbio_SLO_Draft_v1.docx) with suggested language for latency measurement and one proposed remedies clause. Could you confirm the measurement percentile and your reporting preference so we can send a procurement-ready SLO/SLA clause?

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm desired percentile (p95 vs p99) and exclusions by Mon 4/19.
- We update the doc + sizing and hand to procurement for a quoting exercise.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@norbio.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@norbio.com>, procurement@norbio.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Norbio SLO/SLA follow-up — latency measurement, concurrency & reporting

Thanks Jonas — great demo. A couple clarifications from our side so we can align legal/procurement: 

1) Percentile: For the UI team we care about p95 for interactive sessions, but Product Ops wants p99 for any production webhooks (they're high-criticality). Can you support different SLOs by endpoint type?

2) Exclusions: We expect scheduled maintenance (planned >48h notice) to be excluded. What about model upgrades that cause temporary increased latency? We need to understand rollback windows and if those events are excluded.

3) Streaming: Important that partial transcripts arrive in under 250ms for the first token and subsequent tokens stream steadily. Also need a recovery policy if a streaming connection drops mid-session — auto-resume or a way to continue without causing duplicate outputs.

4) Remedies: Procurement prefers credit-based remedies for measurable breach. For severity/incidents that are not clear SLO breaches, they'd prefer an agreed escalation and RCA window (48-72h).

I'll loop in procurement once we have a slightly more prescriptive SLO wording. Also please confirm whether the throughput numbers above require reserved capacity or if Redwood can support burstable capacity with fallbacks (and what the failover behavior would be).

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Engineering, Norbio Therapeutics
samira.khan@norbio.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Norbio SLO/SLA follow-up — latency measurement, concurrency & reporting

Samira — thanks, good notes. Below are concrete answers and a proposed SLO split to satisfy both Product and UI teams. I pasted the relevant redline text into the attached PDF for legal to review.

A) Percentile by endpoint type (proposal):
- Interactive UI endpoints: p95 latency <= 300ms (measured end-to-end at the Redwood edge in the same region as request origin).
- Webhook / critical APIs: p99 latency <= 450ms (measured end-to-end; includes network egress to customer-hosted webhook URL).

B) Exclusions (proposal):
- Scheduled maintenance: excluded if >48 hours notice or agreed maintenance window.
- Model upgrade events: excluded if a pinned model version is being migrated during a defined maintenance window; otherwise treated as non-excluded and measured. We can add a 6-hour warmup window after a model swap where transient higher latency is tolerated for the purpose of immediate SLA breach calculation, but it still counts toward engineering RCA if degraded.

C) Streaming requirements & recovery:
- First-token latency: p95 <= 250ms for first token on new streaming sessions.
- Sustained stream: median inter-token latency <= 180ms for active sessions.
- Recovery: Redwood supports resumable streaming sessions for intermittent disconnects if the client includes the session-id; otherwise we recommend a short-lived dedup token to prevent double-processing. We'll include a short SDK snippet in the final MRP.

D) Throughput & reserved capacity:
- For guaranteed throughput (150 RPS sustained) we recommend reserved capacity (Dedicated pool) sized to the workload; otherwise we can support bursty traffic on hosted with fallback policies (degraded model variant / increased queuing) and transparent throttling. Pricing differs materially — I can scope a reserved-node quote once you confirm tolerance for fallbacks.

E) Remedies & reporting cadence:
- Reporting: automated weekly summary + monthly SLO dashboard export. On detected breach we open an incident and provide a 72-hour RCA.
- Remedies: standard proposal is SLA credits for measurable, verified breaches (formula in SLO draft); for ambiguous incidents we follow escalation ladder with remediation milestones before crediting.

Attached: SLO_clause_redline.pdf with the proposed edits (highlights show the differences for p95/p99 split and the 6-hour warmup note).

If this looks good I will:
1) Update the Norbio_SLO_Draft to include the split p95/p99 and the streaming recovery language.
2) Produce two sizing options (reserved nodes vs hosted burst) and associated TCO estimate for procurement.

Can you confirm the preferred remedy model (credits vs escalation-first) and whether procurement wants the reserved capacity quote before the SLA language is finalized?

Thanks — Jonas

Attachment: SLO_clause_redline.pdf (pdf, 12KB)

Samira — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per your procurement preference, here's a compact summary and proposed next steps: 

Summary (agreed / proposed):
- UI endpoints: p95 <= 300ms (measured at Redwood edge).
- Critical webhooks: p99 <= 450ms (end-to-end).
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance >48h notice excluded; model upgrades get a 6-hour warmup exclusion window for immediate breach calc but are still logged for RCA.
- Streaming: first-token p95 <= 250ms; median inter-token <= 180ms; resumable sessions supported via session-id.
- Remedies: default = credit-based SLA for verified breaches. For incidents that require judgement, we follow escalation ladder and provide RCA within 72h; credits applied after verification.
- Throughput: reserved pool recommended for 150 RPS sustained; hosted burst supported with fallback to degraded variants and throttling.

Requested confirmation (short):
1) Confirm remedy model: "credits as primary" vs "escalation-first".
2) Confirm whether you want reserved pool pricing before legal signs off on SLO language.

Next steps:
- If you confirm credits-as-primary, we'll update the SLO doc and send a procurement packet (1–2 pgs SLO + pricing options + redline).
- Suggested meeting: Tue 4/20 11:00am ET to walk procurement through options (I can send a calendar invite).

If that works, I'll send the updated docs and a short mutual action plan linking the SLO doc, pricing options, and DocuSign placeholders.
